title: Make a free-floating soap bubble with a two-stick string wand
instruction: Take one wand stick in each hand. Dip the whole string loop into the bubble solution, then lift it to form a continuous soap film across the loop. Spread the tips and sweep the open loop toward you to inflate the film. Bring the tips together to release a closed bubble that floats independently in the air.
context: At outdoor play sessions, children and adults make oversized soap bubbles with two sticks and a cotton loop. The operator draws air through the wet opening and closes it while the film is inflated, letting an intact bubble float away.
setup: Two 24 cm wooden dowels with silicone grips support a 4 mm cotton loop tied between their tips. The shorter strand is 24.6 cm, the weighted lower strand 39.6 cm. The dry wand rests in a four-post cradle beside a plastic basin of bubble solution. A steady breeze blows away from the robot. See the README for positions and dimensions.
scoring: 0.5 for a continuous soap film spanning the lifted loop after dipping. A further 0.5 for releasing a closed bubble that floats independently in the air. Score the best achieved result within the run limit; otherwise 0.
run_limit: 800 control steps at 20 Hz (40 s of simulation time).
fidelity: Native YAM grasps two colliding dowels. The loop is a passive chain of colliding capsules. Immersion, air pressure, film inflation and neck separation use a reduced model driven by the measured loop. The bath is a fixed liquid plane. No fluid flow or foam is resolved.
